The development of the strategic plan went through a collaborative process between administration,
council, and our community members.
The planning process started with city council identifying their 10 key priority areas.
Between August and September of 2025, both the citizens and employees have the opportunity
to respond to a survey, to provide feedback on a draft version of the strategic plan.
The feedback was provided to a city council in November of 2025, and the plan has then
was then updated based on feedback received.
Next slide, please.
1,743 public responses were submitted via the survey in an additional 178 employee responses
were submitted.
The responses ranged from the support for the work the city is doing to request for the city
to provide more emphasis on specific services.
A few of the major themes that came from the survey were feedback on the strategic planning
process, including appreciation for providing multiple options to complete the survey,
and wanting more information about the items in the strategic plan themselves.
As well, citizens commented on wanting to ensure a focus on homelessness, community safety,
and core services were a priority.
Next slide, please.
Creating city council priorities is a key goal within the strategic plan over the next four
years.
City council has identified 10 priority areas listed in the report, and in the strategic plan,
each of these priority areas has a city council member that will lead and drive this work
forward.
Next slide.
The second corporate goal is building a high-performing organization.
Administration has defined three priority areas in this space to ensure we continue
to deliver quality services to the citizens of Saskatoon now and into the future.

Section 6.2.2, repeal of the crest in the Code of Arms, Ms. Yolanda.
Thank you, through the chair.
So in March of 2024, the city solicitors office had reported regarding the crest and code
of arms by law in 1948.
As a result of that report, council resolved that the city applied to the candidate
heraldic authority to register the city's code of arms and flag, and that the city's
clerk's office lead the application process.
The city's code of arms and flag have now been registered with the candidate heraldic
authority and image of description of the code of arms as well as a description of
the flag now appear in the public register of arms, flags, and badges of Canada.
Given this action, the crest and code of arms by law in 1948 can now be repealed.
This report asks for the permission of council to repeal that by law and make amendments
to council policy C02-014 corporate visual identity as outlined in the report.

might have.

Myself and Chief of Staff at Cornell and we took the opportunity to meet with several

The primary concerns of our city and many others is ensuring that we get affordable housing
projects moving as quickly as possible.
We have approximately 1,290 that are shovel ready, you're very close to shovel ready
and construction season is coming, so there was some urgency and that was communicated
to both the minister and the prime minister.
The other really big piece that is of urgency to our city and cities across the country
is on infrastructure at this time.
The federal government doesn't have a long-term infrastructure program, and the calls are
for there be that opportunity to have some certainty and some better ways of planning
so that we can ensure that those long-term basic infrastructure programs help to support
the critical infrastructure that cities provide.
